clue.text: It's spite overturned ex-minister Chamberlain, according to his mates

indicators.note: turned upside down, so the two names are read from the far end back to the start

parts.note: Mo Mowlam, the former Northern Ireland Secretary
Neville Chamberlain's friends would shorten his name to Nev

explanation.surface: Somebody claims an old cabinet minister's friends regard him as spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Mowlam was a Labour cabinet minister of the time; 'overturned' reads MO and NEV backwards. 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is malice or bitterness of feeling, a close synonym for spite.

clue.text: Underwear (seconds) to be seen in TV docusoap

indicators.note: something seen in a programme appears inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Vets in Practice and Vets' School were BBC fly-on-the-wall docusoaps, known simply by the word vets

explanation.surface: Somebody spots flashes of underwear on a reality show about animal doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: A docusoap is a British documentary series following real people at work; 'to be seen in' puts S inside VETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vests are sleeveless undershirts in British English, a common item of underclothing.

clue.text: Writer in a bust-up with his one-time proté g

definitions.text: Writer in a bust-up with his one-time proté g

parts.words: Writer in a bust-up with his one-time proté g
parts.note: the novelist famously fell out with Paul Theroux, the younger writer he had once mentored

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a description rather than wordplay: in 1998 Paul Theroux published a bitter memoir of his long friendship with the Nobel-winning Trinidad-born novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: V S Naipaul was the Trinidad-born novelist whose feud with his former disciple Theroux became literary gossip.

clue.text: No Spitting Image without peers

parts.note: a spitting image is an exact double, a perfect match
no means less in the sense of lacking, as in 'no hope' and 'hopeless'

explanation.surface: It suggests the satirical puppet show Spitting Image had no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV show with grotesque puppets of public figures; here the phrase just means an identical copy. 'No' comes first in the clue but its piece goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no peers has no equal anywhere, which is exactly what matchless means.

clue.text: To die-for oral sex and a bang to finish you off?

definitions.text: a bang to finish you off

parts.note: read literally, something you die from is fatal
a blow job, shortened to blow

explanation.surface: A crude boast about sex so good it ends with a satisfying climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To die-for' would normally mean irresistible, but here it is taken literally as deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal blow is the killing strike, and a bang is a hard hit, so the bang that kills you is one.

clue.text: The press is not entitled to even a bronze vehicle

parts.words: not entitled to even a bronze
parts.note: a competitor finishing fourth just misses the bronze medal for third
an estate is the British term for a station wagon

explanation.surface: A sneer that journalists don't deserve any award, set beside a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fourth Estate is the traditional name for journalism as a power alongside the three historic estates of the realm.

clue.text: He's doing it again, the love rat!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, someone who does it twice, a two-time offender
second meaning: a love rat is a tabloid term for an unfaithful partner, one who cheats

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests a tabloid headline about a serial cheat; the first part plays on 'two times'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer deceives a partner by secretly seeing someone else, exactly what tabloids call a love rat.

clue.text: City, lacking capital, haemorrhages

indicators.note: without its capital, that is its first letter, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to haemorrhage is to bleed heavily

explanation.surface: A city short of money is losing it fast, as if bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, but 'lacking capital' means dropping the first letter of BLEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Prosecution's pointless linen costume

indicators.note: without a point of the compass, so one of N, S, E or W is dropped

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen or cotton fabric
north, a compass point
a suit is a set of matching clothes

explanation.surface: A prosecutor apparently dislikes a linen outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' means losing a compass point, so the fabric lawn becomes LAW. The 's after Prosecution stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal action brought in court, and prosecution is bringing such a case.

clue.text: Hack gets out of woollen suit and it's as awful as you can imagine

definitions.text: as awful as you can imagine

indicators.note: leaves, so these letters are removed from the other word

parts.note: worsted is a smooth woollen fabric
a hack is a journalist; ED is the editor
a case or suit is a legal action

explanation.surface: A journalist strips off a wool suit, and the result is ghastly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets out of' removes ED, the editor, from WORSTED to leave WORST; 'suit' looks like clothing but is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The worst-case scenario is the most pessimistic outcome anyone could picture.

clue.text: Oriental treatment dump containing argon — America flips

indicators.note: holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to take a dump is slang for to defecate
A was the original chemical symbol for argon, before Ar

indicators.note: turns over, so the letters of the abbreviation are read backwards

parts.note: US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A massage parlour in a rubbish dump, with America upending everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' puts A, argon's symbol until 1957, inside SHIT to make SHIAT; 'flips' turns US into SU.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese massage therapy that presses points on the body, so a healing method from the East.

clue.text: Unconcealed hostility when Blunt rolled over naked

parts.note: blunt in the sense of frank and outspoken

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: raw as in bare and exposed

explanation.surface: It hints at hostility toward the spy Anthony Blunt after he was exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Blunt with a capital looks like a surname but means frank; 'rolled over' turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Open war is conflict fought openly, so hostility that nobody hides.

clue.text: "Silver" tucked into awful shit pet food

indicators.note: put inside, so one piece sits within the other
something awful is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Somebody condemns a brand of pet food as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet food' looks like the definition, but 'awful' rearranges SHIT PET into SPHETTI, and 'tucked into' puts AG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, a staple foodstuff.

clue.text: Rent-free residence but crap position?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a building occupied without paying rent or having permission
second meaning: the crouching posture, as used when defecating without a toilet

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a poor place to live; 'crap' is vulgar slang, not a judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an occupied empty building and a crouched stance close to the ground.

clue.text: Brilliantly successful line in capital provides Brenda with excuse to get out and about more

definitions.text: provides Brenda with excuse to get out and about more

parts.note: golden as in a golden era or golden boy
the Jubilee line is a London Underground line

explanation.surface: A newly successful Tube line gives the Queen a reason to travel more.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose fifty years on the throne were celebrated in 2002 with nationwide tours.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden jubilee marks fifty years of reign, and the 2002 celebrations sent the monarch touring the country.

clue.text: Lacking energy, Geri's tits — a new-fangled medical condition

indicators.note: made in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style jibe at a pop star's bust as some trendy new ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops the E of energy from GERIS TITS A, and 'new-fangled' rearranges what is left. Geri is Geri Halliwell of the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining, an illness.

clue.text: Opening of video, 'Arse' at Tate provoked bad feeling

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of video
end is a word for the backside

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A video of a backside in the Tate gallery caused a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of' gives V; 'provoked' rearranges TATE into ETTA. The Tate is the London gallery, and 'at' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud marked by bitter hostility.

clue.text: It's hell to MP, getting cut up

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, ruled by Pluto
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Somebody tells an MP that it's hell being cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut a body apart limb by limb.

clue.text: End of condom (or 'Mates') split by little monkey

indicators.note: broken apart, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of condom

explanation.surface: A burst condom of the Mates brand blamed on a small mischievous child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like the condom bursting but signals the anagram, and 'End of' picks the last letter. Mates is a British condom brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmosets are tiny South American primates, among the smallest monkeys.

clue.text: Flannel supplied when erection lost on TV series

parts.note: losing an erection leaves one soft
a soap is a serial drama on TV

explanation.surface: A tale of impotence while watching a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Flannel is British for a face cloth, but here it means smooth insincere talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is flattery used to persuade, which is what flannel means in British slang.

clue.text: Footsie and length contraction with finger

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for feet or foot, a length
the index finger is the forefinger

explanation.surface: Flirting under the table by foot, then moving on to the hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing footsie means flirting with feet; here Footsie is the nickname of the London stock market index.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE 100, the main London share index, is nicknamed Footsie and was formerly called the FT Index.

clue.text: See 4
Plastic chip attached to Clary — "kinky!"

indicators.note: twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: Julian Clary, the camp British comedian
IC stands for integrated circuit, a silicon chip

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a plastic chip given to the camp comic Julian Clary.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic resin used in plastics and fibres.

clue.text: Doughty type has jar (not pissed)

indicators.note: British slang for drunk, so these letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A brave sort has a drink but stays sober.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, a jar is a pint of beer and pissed means drunk. The brackets make 'not pissed' look like a comment, but 'not' joins 'jar' in the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works like a Trojan is resolute and hard-working, so a Trojan is a stalwart sort.

clue.text: Rule of Brenda: leather strap restricts weight

indicators.note: holds something in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a rein is a leather strap for guiding a horse
g stands for gram, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: It pictures the Queen ruling with a whip and a firm hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II; 'restricts' has REIN holding G.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period of her rule.

clue.text: Celebrity poser, single bitch on the up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to bitch is to complain, or moan

explanation.surface: A famous model, unattached and moody, whose career is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi Campbell is a supermodel, someone famous for posing in front of cameras.

clue.text: Give a really pisspoor rendition of an Ice T number and charge!

parts.words: Give a really pisspoor rendition of
parts.note: to murder a song is to sing it terribly
Ice-T is an American rapper, so his songs are raps

explanation.surface: Someone butchers a song by the rapper Ice-T and is accused for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice-T's band also recorded the notorious 'Cop Killer', which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A murder rap is an accusation of homicide, rap being slang for a criminal indictment.

clue.text: Politicians responsible for leaks about Blair's last letter

indicators.note: surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to take a leak is slang for to urinate, so leaks are pees
R is the final letter of Blair

explanation.surface: A dig at politicians who briefed against Tony Blair near the end of his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts PEES around R; 'responsible for' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers are members of the House of Lords, who sit in Parliament as legislators.

clue.text: Outside ramshackle flat

indicators.note: falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Estate agents' shorthand for a run-down apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ramshackle' rearranges OUTSIDE; 'flat' looks like an apartment but means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of lifeless and boring is close to tedious.

clue.text: See 13
Brigitte Bardot no longer to decide if a little creature's male or female

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the film star was the original ... in the 1950s and 60s, but no longer young

definitions.text: to decide if a little creature's male or female
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as a verb phrase, to sex a kitten is to find out its gender

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally, with sex as the vet's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sex kitten is a young woman who plays up her sexual allure, a label coined for Bardot.

clue.text: Topless geriatrics get them off and achieve an orgasm

definitions.text: get them off and achieve an orgasm

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter is removed

parts.note: old crocks are elderly or decrepit people

explanation.surface: Elderly people strip off and enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' drops the C from CROCKS; the definition plays on 'get your rocks off', slang for reaching orgasm.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about reaching climax, the thing one gets off is one's rocks.
